newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU parliament bans ETA representative.
newsitem.headline: EU parliament bans ETA representative.

text.p: The European Parliament, joining the outcry against the Basque separatist group ETA's killing of a young town councillor, on Thursday banned a former Euro-deputy from ETA's political wing.

The EU assembly's political leaders unanimously declared that Karmelo Landa, a leading member of ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna and a member of the European Parliament until 1994, would be refused access to all the parliament's buildings in Brussels, Strasbourg and Luxembourg.
"It was decided to withdraw his access rights...with immediate effect," a spokesman for the parliament's Spanish President Jose-Maria Gil-Robles told Reuters.
Jaume Duch said Landa sometimes took part in press conferences. "He has a right to free speech but we cannot allow him to use the European Parliament to make apologies for terrorism," he said.

A statement issued by Gil-Robles's office on Thursday said the parliament would send a delegation to the Basque country soon to meet the family of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, who was kidnapped by ETA on July 10 and shot 48 hours later.
Basque politicial leaders and the central government in Madrid have vowed to isolate Herri Batasuna because it did not condemn the killing, which sparked nationwide outrage in Spain.
ETA began its armed campaign for an independent state in 1968 under the dictatorship of Francisco Franco, who repressed any expression of Basque nationalism.
Support for the group has waned since Franco's death in 1975 and the subsequent transition to democracy, which eventually gave the Basque region a high degree of autonomy.
